channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indonesia: Post-S&P optimism faces weak risk uptake – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao notes that S&P Global Ratings has retained Indonesia’s sovereign rating and stable outlook, citing fiscal discipline and expectations of rationalized flagship spending and improved revenues.

item.title: Mexican Peso surges as inflation data weighs on the USD
item.description: The Mexican Peso appreciates against the US Dollar during the North American session, up 0.29% after the latest US inflation reports, easing expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise rates to tackle high inflation. At the time of writing, the USD/MXN trades at 17.38

item.title: China: production-led growth with weak demand – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that China’s H1 data show resilient industrial and high‑tech production but weak domestic demand, with retail sales and property investment under pressure.

item.title: Thai Baht: Limited gains as Oil stays elevated – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that USD/THB fell after the post-US Consumer Price Index (CPI) decline in US Dollar (USD) but quickly retraced, signalling limited follow-through in Thai Baht gains.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Consolidation bias holds within tight band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD reversed its New York-session plunge after softer United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI), closing near 1.2910.

item.title: China: Q2 growth slowdown raises policy pressure – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao notes that China’s Q2 2026 GDP growth slowed to 4.3% year-on-year, below Beijing’s 4.5%-5% target and consensus expectations. Fixed-asset investment contracted sharply, while June industrial output and retail sales surprised on the upside.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar extends decline as softer PPI lifts major currencies and Gold
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) falls 0.5% toward 100.40 as softer-than-expected United States (US) wholesale inflation reinforces signs that price pressure is easing. The headline Produce Price Index (PPI) declined 0.3% MoM in June, while the annual rate slowed to 5.5%, below the 6.2% forecast.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Swissie breaks below rising wedge, bears eye 0.8000
item.description: The USD/CHF breaks a rising wedge, tumbles over 0.62%, and trades near three-day lows on Wednesday. The pair clears the July 14 swing low of 0.8067. At the time of writing, the pair trades at 0.8041.

item.title: Asia FX: Softer USD offset by high Oil – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong expect Asian FX to trade with a better tone after softer United States (US) core Consumer Price Index (CPI) reduced near-term Fed hike expectations and pressured USD.

item.title: WTI hovers near one-month high as Hormuz supply risks remain in focus
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Crude Oil consolidates modest losses on Wednesday but stays close to a one-month high as escalating Middle East tensions keep supply risks around the Strait of Hormuz in focus. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $78.70, up roughly 10% so far this week.

item.title: $4,000 under siege: Buyers losing the battle on Gold
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) is under strong selling pressure on Wednesday, yet action around XAU/USD is muted.

item.title: Gold price slips as Iran escalation overshadows soft US PPI
item.description: The Gold price turns negative on Wednesday, even though the last two US inflation reports showed that prices are dropping, though developments in the Middle East sent energy prices higher. At the time of writing, the XAU/USD traded at $4,034, down some 0.53%.

item.title: Euro elevates as softer US PPI weighs on the Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD trades higher near the 1.1450 area on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following softer-than-expected United States (US) Producer Price Index (PPI) data.

item.title: Silver slips as hawkish Fed outlook persists despite soft US inflation data
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades on the back foot on Wednesday, struggling to capitalize on a weaker US Dollar (USD) as hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations keep bears in control. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $57.55, down 1.90% on the day.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average toasts peak inflation, then drops the glass
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) spent most of Wednesday rewarding the disinflation trade and the final two hours dismantling it.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens modestly but remains near multi-decade lows
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) holds modest gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday but struggles to extend its recovery despite a broadly weaker Greenback following softer-than-expected US inflation data. At the time of writing, USD/JPY trades around 162.14, down 0.07% on the day.

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh: Inflation will not be permanent
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh said on Wednesday that current inflation pressure will not be permanent, while acknowledging that the latest inflation measures remain unsatisfactory.

item.title: British Pound rallies as soft US PPI hits US Dollar
item.description: The Pound Sterling rises by some 0.60% against the US Dollar after the latest Producer Price Index (PPI) in the US showed prices edging lower, driven by the dip in energy prices since late May. At the time of writing, the GBP/USD trades at 1.3460 after bouncing off a daily low of 1.3370.

item.title: BoC's Macklem: Canadian Dollar weakness not a factor in rate decisions
item.description: The Bank of Canada (BoC) left its policy rate unchanged at 2.25% on Wednesday, as widely anticipated. Governor Tiff Macklem leaned hawkish in the press conference that followed the announcement, as policymakers seem confident about growth and inflation perspectives.

item.title: Gold steadies as traders balance soft US inflation data against rising Oil prices
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) steadies on Wednesday, erasing intraday losses after softer-than-expected US Producer Price Index (PPI) data push the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields lower.

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh: One-time change in prices isn't necessarily inflationary
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh said on Wednesday that recent inflation figures provide an imperfect measure of underlying inflation. Warsh made the remarks while testifying on the Semiannual Monetary Policy Report before the US Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy urgency and mixed data – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s warning that Japan must build a strong economy now, rejecting claims that an economic blueprint drove the JGB selloff.

item.title: Canadian Dollar shows little reaction to Bank of Canada interest rate decision
item.description: USD/CAD trades flat on Wednesday as traders show a limited reaction to the latest Bank of Canada (BoC) monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.4051, hovering near a one-month low.

item.title: Euro: Energy risks cap upside against US Dollar – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING says EUR/USD rallied on softer US CPI but warns that rising Oil and European natural gas prices limit upside. He expects EUR/USD to struggle above 1.1460/70 and potentially retreat toward 1.1360/80 if Oil gains another leg higher.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: June CPI consistent with progress on inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of New York President John Williams said on Wednesday that the latest United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) report was consistent with the inflation progress he hopes to see over the coming months.

item.title: Australian Dollar rises amid softer US PPI
item.description: AUD/USD trades higher near the 0.7000 level on Wednesday as the Australian Dollar (AUD) benefits from broad US Dollar (USD) weakness following softer-than-expected United States (US) producer inflation data.

item.title: US Dollar: Limited downside after CPI – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes the Dollar has steadied after its post-CPI slide, with US economic outperformance, a higher-for-longer Federal Reserve stance and strong foreign demand for US securities limiting further downside.

item.title: British Pound: Honeymoon risks for Pound – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses the British Pound's (GBP) strong performance, noting GBP is the second-best G10 currency over three months despite no Bank of England (BoE) hikes.

item.title: Euro finds support as soft US PPI weighs on US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD recovers its intraday losses on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) comes under pressure after the latest US inflation data surprised to the downside. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1430 after hitting an intraday low of 1.1406.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Year-end weakness forecast against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Mauricio Une and Renan Alves note that the US Dollar (USD) ended the previous week at Brazilian Real (BRL) 5.1086, with the Brazilian Real appreciating 1.2% and ranking third among 24 emerging currencies.
